'''''Exochorda racemosa''''', the '''pearlbush''' or '''common pearlbush''', is a species of plant in the family [[Rosaceae]]. This species is mostly found in [[China]] and [[Japan]].<ref name=Levy>{{cite book|last=Ran Levy-Yamamori, Gerard Taaffe|title=Garden plants of Japan|year=2004|publisher=Timber Press|location=USA|isbn=0-88192-650-7|page=109}}</ref>

==Taxonomy and etymology==

''Exochorda racemosa'' was first [[Species description|described]] by [[John Lindley]]. It is placed in the [[genus]] ''[[Exochorda]]'' and family [[Rosaceae]], the rose family.<ref name=powell>{{cite book|author1=William C. Welch|title=Heirloom gardening in the South : yesterday's plants for today's gardens|publisher=Texas A&M University Press|isbn=978-1-60344-213-8|edition=1st|author2=Greg Grant|author3=Cynthia W. Mueller|author4=Jason Powell|date=7 April 2011}}</ref>  The plant gets its common name, "common pearlbush", from its pearl-looking flowers.<ref name=Dirr>{{cite book|last=Dirr|first=Michael|title=Dirr's Hardy trees and shrubs: an illustrated encyclopedia|year=1997|publisher=[[Timber Press]]|location=USA|isbn=0-88192-404-0|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=CmKi3t5qZe4C&q=Exochorda+racemosa&pg=PA154|page=154|format=PDF|quote=The expanding buds appear as small pearls - hence, the common name.}}</ref>

==Description==
[[File:Pearlbush Exochorda racemosa Leaf Stalk 2000px.jpg|thumb|left|150px|The [[foliage]] of ''E. racemosa''.]]
A loose, irregular or vase-shaped and upright [[shrub]], this species is [[deciduous]]. It has oblong leaves, about {{convert|4|-|6|cm|in|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|1|-|2|cm|in|abbr=on}} wide, that are rounded and toothed at the margin on the top. The flowers are white, and flower in late April to early May.<ref name=Woody>{{cite web|last=Kling|first=Gary J.|title=Exochorda racemosa Common pearlbush|url=http://woodyplants.nres.uiuc.edu/plant/exora|work=University of Illinois|publisher=Woody Plants}}</ref> The flowers have round [[petal]]s, 12-25 [[stamen]]s, borne in racemes in groups of about six or ten. Their diameter is {{convert|4|cm|in|abbr=on}}. Flowers give way to brown, dehiscent seed capsules.<ref name="NC State">{{Cite web|title=Exochorda racemosa (Common Pearlbush, Pearlbush) {{!}} North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox|url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/exochorda-racemosa/|access-date=2021-02-25|website=plants.ces.ncsu.edu}}</ref>
